variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Finish all memory updates from the observed interval before selecting the next command. Dispatch exclusively on the resulting buttons_completed value: if 0, choose A, press the first button; if 1, choose B, press the second button; if 2, neither A nor B is eligible and use the container-handling rules below. Never select a button using the incoming count after updating it, or because a completed button has sprung back. At the initial decision the initialized count is 0, so choose A. Determine whether a container is currently held from the latest decision scene, using earlier frames only to interpret the transition. A container held earlier in the interval is no longer held after observed release onto the table and withdrawal of the open gripper. With both presses completed, an empty hand at the decision scene, and a nonempty pending_target_positions list, choose C pointing inside the visible container identified by its first entry; use its current center rather than requiring an exact historical pixel. With a container still held at the decision scene and further pending targets, choose D to free the hand. The successful lift has already removed the completed target from the list, so after D finishes and the hand is empty, choose C for the new first entry, not the container just replaced. These rules produce A, B, C for single-target goals and A, B, C, D, C for two-target goals. Completion is reached upon successfully lifting the final requested container; the supplied episodes end with that final pickup command. If another decision is nevertheless requested with an empty target list and a held container, choose D. For an unanticipated ambiguous situation, preserve facts not contradicted by observations and prefer the best trajectory-consistent match for the pending target. Retry only a button press or pickup not established as completed. This fallback must never override observed completion, restore a removed target, or permit A or B when the updated buttons_completed is 2. If no target remains and an action is still mandatory with an empty hand, use D as the non-pickup fallback.

fields.name: pending_target_positions
fields.description: With empty incoming memory, read the requested colors in goal order and initialize an ordered list of their visible cube centers as [y, x]. Otherwise start with the incoming list. At every decision, including one whose next command is another button press, process all observed frames chronologically before writing memory or selecting a command. Associate each exposed target cube with the container descending over it, then follow that container through all observed motion, including residual motion during later pickup or put-down intervals. Track contents with moving containers; never reassign a color solely because a container returns to an original cube location. Seed target identities from incoming positions, which are anchors at the preceding decision scene, not coordinates required to appear exactly in the first new frame. If motion has already begun by that frame, associate the displaced candidates jointly with those anchors using their initial displacement and the subsequent observed pair motion. Resolve this initial association consistently with the later trajectory, then propagate the assigned identities through the entire interval. Never snap an identity back to its incoming position merely because another container occupies it. For newly covered cubes, use the association with their descending covers. For each rotating pair, temporarily track both members, including any non-target partner. Estimate their shared center, using the pair midpoint solely as a temporary rotation reference, never as a target position. Anchor both identities at their pre-motion positions and use the first small, distinguishable displacement to establish their angular direction around that center. Then, at each successive observed frame, compare the two possible joint assignments using both members' signed angular displacements about the shared center. Among assignments consistent with the established rotation direction, select the smallest common forward angular advance consistent with the preceding motion, rather than an assignment requiring an additional half-turn between adjacent samples. Resolve both identities jointly, not by independently minimizing endpoint distance. Propagate each assigned identity from that frame into the next; do not restart association from its pre-motion position when the pair settles. Carry the resulting identities into the next frame and through the final settling frames. Returning to the same unordered pair of positions must not reset identities: one observed half-turn exchanges them, and two observed half-turns restore them. Apply this procedure to each subsequent moving pair, carrying forward any target identity from earlier exchanges even when its partner changes. These temporary partner tracks do not add persistent memory fields. Perform this tracking even when the button count already determines the next command, and preserve the remaining targets' goal order when writing their updated positions. Update every remaining entry to its container's center in the decision scene, including stationary targets whose cube centers must be replaced by their covering containers' centers. Once covered, every output entry must identify an actual observed container at that scene, never a pair midpoint or an interpolated trajectory position. Process all observed motion, including motion before the next button makes contact, before writing these centers. If the interval shows the first pending container being grasped and lifted successfully, remove that entry once; a held-container observation continuing into a put-down interval is not a new pickup. Recognize success from the grasp-and-lift transition, supported by the revealed requested cube. Keep tracking the remaining targets during the hand's movements, ignoring small occlusion-induced center wobble. Write [] when none remain. e.g. [[111, 128], [82, 155]]
fields.annotation: An ordered list of [y, x] positions identifying the containers for the cube colors requested in the goal, in goal order, excluding targets already successfully picked up. Before covering, use the visible cube centers. Once covered, follow the identity of the covering container through every shuffle, recording its center at the decision scene; contents travel with the container, not with the original table location. Use the complete motion trajectory, not nearest matching between shuffle endpoints. Remove the first entry at the decision step showing its successful pickup, before any subsequent put-down. Track remaining entries during pickup and put-down despite small apparent center shifts.  An empty list means all requested pickups have occurred. e.g. [[111, 128], [82, 155]]

fields.name: buttons_completed
fields.description: Initialize to 0 with empty incoming memory. Start from the incoming count and inspect the entire observed interval for completion of the next required button press. A hand descent to that button followed by withdrawal, with button depression or contact-height evidence, increments the count once, capped at 2. Write this updated count before selecting a command. In particular, incoming 1 plus a completed second press yields 2 even if the button has sprung back in the decision scene. The first menu button is the larger-x button in these scenes; the second is the smaller-x button. A pressed-down label is sufficient supporting evidence but is not mandatory: low contact followed by withdrawal also establishes the press. Preserve the count when buttons spring back and throughout container manipulation. Do not increment merely because a button is visible. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: The number of required button presses completed so far, written as 0, 1, or 2. Record 0 at the initial decision, 1 at the decision following the first button press, and 2 at the decision following the second button press and thereafter. Count completed presses, not buttons currently appearing depressed. e.g. 1

initial.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Update memory from the observed interval before selecting the next command. Every episode starts with A. If buttons_completed is 0, choose A, press the first button. If it is 1, choose B, press the second button. Only when it is 2 may container pickup begin. With both presses completed and no container currently held, choose C pointing inside the visible container identified by the first entry of pending_target_positions; use its current center rather than requiring an exact historical pixel. With a container held and further pending targets, choose D to free the hand. The successful lift has already removed the completed target from the list, so after D finishes and the hand is empty, choose C for the new first entry, not the container just replaced. These rules produce A, B, C for single-target goals and A, B, C, D, C for two-target goals. Completion is reached upon successfully lifting the final requested container; the supplied episodes end with that final pickup command. If another decision is nevertheless requested with an empty target list and a held container, choose D. For an unanticipated ambiguous situation, preserve facts not contradicted by observations, prefer the best trajectory-consistent match for the pending target, and retry an uncompleted button or pickup rather than declaring success without evidence. If no target remains and an action is still mandatory with an empty hand, use D as the non-pickup fallback.

history.critique:
field pending_target_positions, POLICY PROMPT
  When button execution covered the requested cubes and rotated pairs of containers, the policy sometimes correctly chose the next button but retained original cube positions or matched targets to their original endpoints. In other cases it selected the wrong container after both presses. The annotated list instead followed the identities through the exchange. This breaks PREDICTABILITY and, when pickup is due, SUFFICIENCY. Keep the existing ordered list of current positions of requested containers not yet successfully lifted, but make its update procedure explicit: on every decision, including decisions whose next command is another button press, process all observed motion before writing the list. Associate exposed cubes with their descending covers. For a rotating pair, estimate its shared center and follow each member's angular progression around that center across the intermediate frames. Resolve associations jointly for both members, continuing the observed rotation direction rather than independently choosing the nearest endpoint. Returning to the same unordered pair of table positions does not mean the identities returned; a half-turn exchanges them, and successive exchanges must each be applied. Continue tracking through any residual motion in later pickup intervals. For example, a target cover starting at [128, 122], passing through [132, 104] and [122, 89], and finishing opposite its start must be recorded at [104, 94], giving [[104, 94]], even when the next command is still B. A subsequent observed exchange can move that same target back to [128, 122]. Stationary pending targets must also be updated from cube centers to cover centers, and every list entry must be written at its decision-scene position. Preserve the existing successful-lift removal rule: remove the first entry once upon an observed grasp and lift, not on a failed grasp or a continuing held-object observation during put-down.

field buttons_completed, POLICY PROMPT
  After an interval visibly showed contact with the second button, its depressed state, and withdrawal, the policy sometimes retained 1 and chose B again, although the annotated count was 2. This is a PREDICTABILITY failure that also produced an incorrect subgoal. Retain the field as the number of completed required presses, with values 0, 1, and 2. Clarify the update ordering: start from the incoming count, recognize the completed contact-and-withdrawal event anywhere in the observed interval, increment once, and write the updated count before applying action-selection rules. In particular, incoming 1 plus an observed completed second press yields 2, even if the button has sprung back in the final scene. Depression is sufficient supporting evidence; low contact followed by withdrawal also qualifies. Preserve 2 throughout subsequent container manipulation. Example value: 2.

the policy prompt for subgoal
  When both presses had visibly completed, the policy sometimes chose B again, including a case where it correctly wrote buttons_completed=2 and retained the correct target positions. The available memory and observation were sufficient, but the action did not use the updated count, defeating the intended SUFFICIENCY of the selection rules. Make the existing update-before-selection requirement an explicit exclusive dispatch: first finish all memory updates from the observed interval; then use only the resulting count for button selection. Choose A if that count is 0 and B if it is 1. If it is 2, neither A nor B is eligible merely because the incoming count was smaller or a button has sprung back. With count 2 and an empty hand, choose C at the current container identified by the first updated pending position. With a held container and remaining targets, choose D; successful lifting has already removed the lifted target. Preserve the existing completion handling. Restrict the retry fallback to events not established as completed; it must never override observed completion or the count-2 branch.

refused
  Do not add episode-specific trajectory clauses or hard-coded endpoint tables to either document. The reported exchanges share one failure mechanism—original-position or nearest-endpoint matching instead of continuing the rotating pair's motion—and are addressed by the general tracking procedure. The annotations already follow that procedure and remove targets on successful lift, so no annotation-field change or extra memory field is warranted. The initial response that chose A and recorded the requested red and blue cube centers in goal order with count 0 was semantically correct; its only visible difference was spacing inside coordinate lists. That is not a SUFFICIENCY, PREDICTABILITY, or NECESSITY failure and does not justify changing the memory definition.

field pending_target_positions, POLICY PROMPT
  When the goal required identifying covered cubes after both button presses, rotating pairs returned to approximately the same unordered positions while their contents exchanged places. After the first press the policy correctly selected the second button but sometimes wrote the targets at their original locations, unlike the annotated memory. After the second press the same error sometimes selected the wrong first container or left the later target at its pre-exchange location. These are PREDICTABILITY failures and, when the first target is affected, SUFFICIENCY failures. Retain this field as the ordered list of current [y, x] positions of requested containers not yet successfully lifted, but make the existing rotation instruction an explicit tracking procedure: seed target identities from incoming positions, associate exposed cubes with their descending covers, and process every observed frame in chronological order. For each moving pair, temporarily track both members, including a non-target partner. Estimate their common center and compare the two possible joint assignments at each successive frame. Select the assignment that continues the angular direction established by the preceding motion, rather than independently minimizing endpoint distance. Carry those identities forward through the final settling frames. A return of the unordered pair to its starting positions must not reset identities. One observed half-turn exchanges the identities; two observed half-turns restore them. Apply this procedure again to every subsequent rotating pair, even when the next command is already determined by the button count, and keep tracking residual motion during manipulation. At the decision scene, write every remaining target's current center in unchanged goal order. For example, a target moving from [134, 173] through [125, 156] and [109, 151] to [99, 166] must yield [[99, 166]], not the opposite endpoint near its starting position. Remove the first entry only upon an observed successful grasp-and-lift, and preserve that removal during put-down. No additional persistent field is needed.

refused

Pass on a shared operational tracking clarification, not separate rules keyed to particular colors, positions, or button numbers. Do not change the annotator prompt: its current values already follow the observed container identities, including exchanging two requested targets and moving a previously exchanged target through a different pair. Do not change the policy prompt for subgoal or buttons_completed: the failed cases either chose the correct button with incorrect target memory, chose a wrong container because that memory was not updated through the shuffle, or retained an incorrect later-target position despite choosing the correct first container. In one case this sent the final pickup to the wrong container. This breaks PREDICTABILITY for the updated positions and SUFFICIENCY for subsequent target selection. Retain the ordered list of pending target centers and the existing successful-lift removal rule, but make rotation assignment operationally explicit. At the start of an interval, treat incoming target positions as anchors from the preceding decision, not as coordinates that must appear exactly in the first new frame. Associate displaced first-frame candidates jointly with those anchors using the first-frame displacement and the subsequent observed pair motion; continue that assignment through the whole interval. For successive pair observations, compare joint assignments by signed angular advance in the established direction, allowing the smaller forward advance even when nearest-distance matching would imply a backward move. Carry identities through settling; an unordered layout recurring after a half-turn exchanges identities, not restores them. Never snap an identity back to its incoming location merely because that location becomes occupied. For example, an incoming moving target at [121, 159] can first appear at [112, 152], continue through [97, 151] and [95, 169], and settle at [95, 172]; with a stationary first target the output is [[92, 116], [95, 172]]. Update all pending targets before dispatching any command, even when their positions do not affect that command. These are temporary within-interval associations, not additional persistent fields.

applied.refused: No annotation-rule change is committed: its complete-trajectory identity tracking already defines the correct annotations, and the report requests preserving those values. Half-turn exchange and restoration after two observed half-turns are already explicit in the policy prompt. variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Update memory from the observed interval before selecting the next command. Every episode starts with A. If buttons_completed is 0, choose A, press the first button. If it is 1, choose B, press the second button. Only when it is 2 may container pickup begin. With both presses completed and no container currently held, choose C pointing inside the visible container identified by the first entry of pending_target_positions; use its current center rather than requiring an exact historical pixel. With a container held and further pending targets, choose D to free the hand. The successful lift has already removed the completed target from the list, so after D finishes and the hand is empty, choose C for the new first entry, not the container just replaced. These rules produce A, B, C for single-target goals and A, B, C, D, C for two-target goals. Completion is reached upon successfully lifting the final requested container; the supplied episodes end with that final pickup command. If another decision is nevertheless requested with an empty target list and a held container, choose D. For an unanticipated ambiguous situation, preserve facts not contradicted by observations, prefer the best trajectory-consistent match for the pending target, and retry an uncompleted button or pickup rather than declaring success without evidence. If no target remains and an action is still mandatory with an empty hand, use D as the non-pickup fallback.

fields.name: pending_target_positions
fields.description: With empty incoming memory, read the requested colors in goal order and initialize an ordered list of their visible cube centers as [y, x]. Otherwise start with the incoming list. Process the observed frames chronologically: associate each exposed target cube with the container descending over it, then follow that container through the observed motion. Track contents with moving containers; never reassign a color solely because a container returns to an original cube location. Resolve the rotating pairs using trajectory continuity and direction across all intermediate frames, allowing identities to exchange endpoints; nearest endpoint matching alone is incorrect. Update each remaining entry to its container's center in the decision scene.
